prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1468; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at an intersection, with the insured vehicle struck on the driver's side. The insured reported a neck strain and advised that the claimant is now represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and the coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Two independent witnesses gave statements describing the same sequence of events.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photographs and the other driver's statement, both of which match the described impact. The damage pattern on the vehicle is consistent with a side impact at the angle reported.

Entry 5: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account matched what was given at the scene and in the initial report, with no changes in the details.

Entry 6: Received the medical records and bills from the treating provider. The reported neck strain is a plausible injury for a collision of this type, and no earlier injury to that body area appears in the prior records.

Entry 7: Inspected the vehicle and noted a few old scratches near the damaged panel. These may be older than this collision, so the repair estimate has been set aside for a closer look at those areas.

Entry 8: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the treating notes explain the reasons for the extended care. Requested a peer review of the treatment timeline to confirm the length of care is reasonable.

Entry 9: Peer review is pending, and the file is being kept open while counsel provides the requested updates. Reserves remain in place until the review and the repair estimate are finalized.
